positioning.category: Independent WebGPU compiler and runtime for existing applications
positioning.promise: Deliver independently usable WGSL compilation and native WebGPU execution; earn adoption through separately measured compiler or application value.
positioning.governingQuestion: Does the selected compiler or runtime surface preserve its declared semantics and materially improve its consumer outcome under independent evidence?

independenceBoundary.rule: The WGSL compiler and native WebGPU runtime can earn adoption independently; neither requires the other. Doppler owns models and inference. Independent installation, a real consumer requirement and retained use guide bounded work. Browser replacement is optional and separately selected; prepared-program integration is a separate treatment.
requiredEvidence: externally owned non-Doppler consumer of the selected compiler or runtime surface
independent semantic oracle, pinned inputs and reproducible installation
separately measured compiler or runtime advantage against the strongest eligible controls
voluntary maintainer adoption and retention across another release or workload
production signer authorization independent of the execution provider

surfaces.job: Provide independently usable WGSL analysis and target lowering. Evaluate compilation latency, diagnostics, supported shader semantics and generated-program performance separately from runtime execution.
surfaces.promotionGate: A concrete external compiler consumer verifies its declared outcome against independent controls and retains use without requiring DoeRuntime. New campaigns need explicit opportunity selection; closed browser transformations stay closed.

surfaces.job: Own WebGPU validation, resources, submission, completion, memory, synchronization and application integration. Runtime adoption does not require independent adoption of the owned compiler.
surfaces.promotionGate: A frozen non-Doppler application demonstrates a material advantage over the strongest eligible controls; declared-program changes are disclosed; external adoption and repeat retention remain independently evidenced.

surfaces.job: Qualify provider identity, correctness, fallback, replay, lifecycle, and release admissibility without requiring runtime replacement.
surfaces.promotionGate: Qualify incumbent and DoeRuntime impartially with independent output validation, provider identity, explicit fallback, and replay; this feature does not itself prove runtime adoption.

surfaces.job: Retain experimental browser integration as an optional, separately selected adoption route after native wins and application transfer.
surfaces.promotionGate: Requires explicit prioritization, prior transferred runtime application wins and separately hash-bound browser integration with unchanged causal controls.

surfaces.job: Turn retained physical failures into minimized reproductions, candidate corrections, and permanent regression gates.
surfaces.promotionGate: A retained field failure produces a reusable qualified correction without weakening evidence or promotion rules.

commercialOffer.promise: Earn voluntary use through independently measured ordinary provider-substitution advantage; optional declared computation remains a separate treatment. Supported embedding, binaries and support remain commercial hypotheses; independent installation, a real consumer requirement and retained use precede expansion of paid offerings. Payment is not a technical-release prerequisite.

comparators.eligibilityRule: Run only workloads supported by the documented product boundary; retain persistent authentication, WebGL, video, and real TLS bot-handshake rows as ineligible rather than scoring them as losses.

suites.purpose: Compare complete product outcomes on tasks supported by every admitted product.
Test whether endpoint ownership creates material application value beyond a remote stateless service.

decisionRules: K0 remains separate from A, B, C, and D because it changes execution location and service architecture rather than one component.
If K0 wins shared tasks and customers assign no material value to the local-persistent suite, Fawn is not promoted as a product.
B must beat A before Fawn earns standalone value; C must beat B before DoeRuntime earns browser execution; D must beat C before the Direct Protocol survives.
An ineligible K0 row is retained as an eligibility result and never scored as a Fawn win.

forbiddenInferences: DoeProof value does not imply DoeRuntime ownership.
Fawn shell value does not imply DoeRuntime or Direct Protocol value.
K0 is an external product comparator and never identifies the value of an internal Fawn or DoeRuntime component.
Cloudflare documentation and vendor measurements define comparator scope but do not constitute Doe or Fawn execution evidence.
A K0 limitation or ineligible row does not imply Fawn product value.
K0 is an external product comparator and never a fifth A/B/C/D causal lane.
DoeProof value and qualification cannot depend on Doppler availability or provider preference.
A component timing win does not imply an application win.
Node, native, Apple, AMD, browser, and Windows evidence never inherit promotion from one another.
A first qualification does not establish recurring commercial demand.
Paid qualification, DoeProof receipts, compiler breadth, internal benchmarks, and Doppler interoperability cannot substitute for DoeRuntime adoption.
Compiler adoption does not establish native runtime adoption, or conversely.
Verified elimination under a prospective application-replacement contract cannot relabel historical fixed-operation results.
Local isolated installation does not establish external operator reproduction or retained adoption.

reusableProgram.initialScope: Explicit fixed-shape buffer compute; source and shape changes invalidate affected state.
reusableProgram.demonstrationGate: Independent numerical parity, meaningful predeclared application outcome against persistent Dawn and wgpu, lifecycle and memory evidence, AMD Vulkan to Apple Metal reproduction, and transfer to another application.
reusableProgram.adoptionBoundary: Repository demonstrations do not establish external voluntary adoption or retention.

executionOwnership.operatingObjective: Prioritize independent installation of the existing Vulkan integration, one real consumer requirement and retained use. Ordered acceptance milestones do not block correctness, packaging or useful engineering. No successor benchmark is selected automatically.
executionOwnership.expansionPrerequisite: Finish each selected Vulkan batch before selecting another. Existing backend regressions do not constitute parallel optimization campaigns. New compiler work needs a concrete opportunity. Expand support through explicit prioritization and separate physical qualification; customer payment is not a prerequisite for technical progress.

provingSet.applicationRule: Unchanged applications and independent correctness references; Doppler exposes inference problems, while another framework establishes independent adoption.
provingSet.measurementRule: Freeze complete-operation scope, primary advantage and regression limits before execution; retain startup, resident costs, responsiveness, uncertainty and raw samples.

developmentEffectiveness.start: Timestamp of a retained reproducible problem with pinned source and inputs.
developmentEffectiveness.stop: Timestamp of independently verified improvement against frozen correctness and application acceptance.
developmentEffectiveness.recordingRule: Record elapsed time and evidence links in existing work records; retain unresolved and rejected attempts separately. No new measurement framework is required.
developmentEffectiveness.engineeringRule: Keep compiler, backends and host adapters independently testable. Reuse, refactoring and agent assistance serve the ordered milestones; avoid abstractions that add execution overhead.
